text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA
- Meeting postponed between Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic and Serb member in Bosnia's presidency Momcilo Krajisnik; no compromise yet in dispute between the two sides.

- According to a poll conducted by Mark-Plan agency, the majority of Yugoslavs show most confidence in Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, followed by Serbian Radical Party president Vojislav Seselj, consider their living standards poor and future uncertain.

- Montenegrin Democratic Party of Socialists municipal board excluded 15 members of the main board who voted in favour of sacking of DPS president Momir Bulatovic. DPS Cetinje and Niksic municipal boards welcomed Bulatovic's removal.
- The text of the memorandum on the succession of ex-Yugoslavia could be adjusted by end of year, said international mediator Sir Arthur Watts in interview.
- German Berthelsmann foundation offers to mediate in Serb-Kosovo Albanian talks and considers time has come for compromises in Kosovo.
- Considerable progress made in talks on determining the Yugoslav-Macedonian border, said head of Macedonian commission Branko Stojanovic.
POLITIKA
- Both houses of the Yugoslav parliament will hold an extraordinary session on Tuesday to determine candidates for Yugoslav president.

- Serbian parliament continues discussion on electoral laws on Monday. Parliament Speaker Dragan Tomic accused opposition Democratic Party of obstructing work of the republican parliament and preventing adoption of the laws by submitting over 1,600 amendments.
- Nis Tobacco industry DIN has suspended its production because booming black market stifles its sales.

- Serbia's Development Fund will extend 100 million German marks credit to the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency to pay farmers for purchased 1997 wheat crop, to be repaid to the Fund by November 30 mainly from wheat exports, said Federal Agriculture Minister Nedeljko Sipovac.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- Armed clashes between Yugoslav army and Albanian smugglers on the Yugoslav-Albanian border increasingly frequent. Under cover of cigarette smuggling Albanians actually bringing arms into Yugoslavia.
BORBA

- Two Chinese corporations sign $19 million deal with chemicals industry HIP Azotara of Pancevo for equipping a plant for the production of mineral fertilisers with a capacity of 300,000 tonnes per year.
- If used to stimulate production and exports, the foreign capital invested in PTT Srbije should enable economic growth to double, says Serbian Chamber of Commerce official Rajko Uncanin.
- Agriculture in the past five years contributed largely to social peace in the country and therefore deserves greater support, says Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- No customs duties on border crossings between eastern Slavonia in Croatia and Yugoslavia on milk, meat, meat products, rice, sugar, detergents, agricultural machinery. In future, customs to be paid on crude oil from Yugoslavia. Yugoslavs can still enter the region with ID cards only.
BLIC
- Serbian Orthodox Church Patriarch Pavle in Bosnian Serb Republic appeals for harmony and understanding, says quarrels and splits among Serbs lead to ruin.

- Sandzak Moslem leader Sulejman Ugljanin condemns police decision to ban Moslem National Council assembly, says imposing emergency administration in Novi Pazar municipality equals police dictatorship.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- The local board of the Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) in Podgorica expelled 15 members of the party's main board including DPS deputy presidents Milo Djukanovic and Milica Pejanovic-Djurisic.

- Decisions of the local DPS board in Podgorica are not valid, said Pejanovic-Durisic who was elected new party president at the main board session on Friday. The DPS party congress convened by ex-party president Momir Bulatovic can only be a congress of a new party, not the DPS, said Pejanovic-Djurisic.
- If dry weather continues the Ulcinj salt fields will have a record production of 30,000 tonnes of salt this year.
-- Belgrade newsroom 381 11 311 4305
